options.why_wrong: 'So' expresses a simple result, not a conditional result. The stem is a conditional that needs a result clause with 'would'.

options.text: it has been competitive since last year.
options.why_wrong: A present perfect statement describes a fact, not the hypothetical result of an unreal past condition.

options.text: it would have been competitive last year.
options.why_wrong: This is a third conditional referring to the past, which conflicts with the present time reference 'today' implied by a mixed conditional.

options.text: it would be far more competitive today.

grammar_focus: Mixed conditionals: past condition with present result
explanation: The stem uses the past perfect in the if-clause, which refers to an unreal past condition. A mixed conditional then uses 'would' plus a base verb in the main clause to describe the present result. Learners often transfer the same tense from the if-clause to the main clause, so they may choose a past form that does not match the present time reference.
